concept.title: An embedding: a map reference for meaning
concept.shortdesc: An embedding turns a piece of text into a position, so that texts with similar meanings land close together.

conbody.p: Think of an embedding as a reference on a very large map. “Gentle stretching class” and “chair-based yoga” share almost no words, but they land in the same neighbourhood. “Debt advice” lands a long way off.
The real map has around a thousand directions, not two, but the idea is the same. Closeness on the map stands for similarity of meaning.

fig.title: A map of meaning: similar services sit close together

image.alt: Dots representing listings form four groups: gentle exercise, help with food, money advice, and company and conversation. Two listings, a Christmas market and a parish council page, fit no group. A search for somewhere calm to exercise after having a baby lands beside the gentle exercise group.

conbody.p: This is what lets a computer treat “somewhere calm to exercise after having a baby” as a request for something like postnatal yoga, though the two phrases have no words in common.
